confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'The most likely cause now is a defrost system fault' and 'Yes, you do need to do the full manual defrost' despite one yoghurt freezing after 2 days of improvement

rationale: The first fixes (turn the dial down, clear the vents) were right and the customer reported improvement. The assistant then jumped to a defrost-system fault and insisted on a 24-hour manual defrost, even though only one yoghurt at the very back froze after two days. The expected path was to monitor with a thermometer and call an engineer only if freezing persisted. It also repeated the defrost instruction three times and said 'no need to wait for it to cool down' before loading food, which is dubious advice. The 'it is not normal' claim was overconfident given the real uncertainty. It never suggested a thermometer, a few more days of monitoring, or an engineer if freezing continued.
